Squash___Powdery_mildew.Scientific_Name: Podosphaera xanthii (syn. Sphaerotheca fuliginea) and Erysiphe cichoracearum
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Environment: Warm temperatures (20–30°C), moderate to high humidity and poor air circulation. Unlike many fungal diseases, free water on leaves is not required.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Spread: Airborne fungal spores spread rapidly by wind and infected plant material.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Description: Powdery Mildew is one of the most common diseases affecting squash and other cucurbits. It reduces photosynthesis by covering leaves with a white powdery fungal growth, resulting in lower fruit yield and poor fruit quality.

Age_Cycle.Early: Small white powdery spots appear on upper leaf surfaces.
Age_Cycle.Moderate: White fungal growth spreads across both sides of leaves causing yellowing.
Age_Cycle.Severe: Leaves become brown, dry and die prematurely, reducing fruit development.
Age_Cycle.Estimated: Symptoms usually become visible within 5–10 days after infection under favorable conditions.

Treatment: Apply fungicides at the first sign of infection.
Prevention: Remove infected plant debris after harvest.
Monitor plants weekly during warm weather.
Recommended_Actions: Begin fungicide applications at early infection.
